photograph.author: Olivier Dugornay (Ifremer)
photograph.description: The crab is found in the North Sea, the English Channel, the North-East Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Its shell measures 5 to 6 cm in length and 8 cm in width. It is brownish in colour, with appendages with blue lines and bright red eyes. There are 4 to 5 teeth on the shell on either side of the eyes. Its hind legs, called "swimming legs", have a characteristic flattened shape. Here we see two individuals in the reproductive phase: the male embraces the female during her moulting period, the only period when she is receptive. This embrace can be long. The reproductive period is between February and November. A pink carpet of anemone corinactis, also called jewel anemone, surrounds the crabs. This anemone is present in the English Channel, the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Its color is often bright, with slightly translucent tentacles with a more colorful bulge at their end. Most of the individuals photographed here are closed.

sources.scope: Selected descriptions on printed3–6 read; actual neotype frontal/dorsal figure on printed7 rendered and viewed. Notched front, unequal lobes/denticles, five side teeth, short hair, ridged unequal chelae/black cutting edges and pointed final paddles guide this authored geometry. shape.before: The withheld generic oval/rod-limbed draft and its concrete shortcomings remain shown in the comparison sheet.
shape.changed: A flatter regional shell has five forward side teeth per side, a median frontal incision, paired larger lobes and intervening small denticles. Strong unequal ridged chelae, black cutting edges, red eyes, six pointed supports and two articulated sharp-tipped paddles replace the generic oval and rod limbs.
shape.remaining: Frontal denticle counts vary; the authored positions, widths, shell profile and limb ratios are unmeasured. Pubescence density, ridge granules, mouthparts, ventral plates, gills and pleopods remain simplified. The licensed photo shows an embracing pair; the model is a single supported male morphology study, without mating or moulting.

surface.changed: Attached short dense instanced setae give the brown shell a velvet surface. Chela hair and raised blue/purple ridge cues, darker fingers, regional numerical cuticle pigment and microrelief are retained across actions.
surface.remaining: Original numerical illustration, not a scan, calibrated albedo, measured cuticle optics or full species variation. Frontal denticle counts vary; the authored positions, widths, shell profile and limb ratios are unmeasured. Pubescence density, ridge granules, mouthparts, ventral plates, gills and pleopods remain simplified. The licensed photo shows an embracing pair; the model is a single supported male morphology study, without mating or moulting.

movement.changed: Same geometry and materials across a short authored lateral bout with planted support and lifted recovery, local chela/antennule handling, finger opening, quiet support and Observe reset. The P5 pair has a stationary articulated paddle loop, with walking legs carried.
movement.remaining: No species-measured coordinates, biological frequency, joint limits, forces, fluid dynamics, sensory physiology, food contact or ingestion. No validated sleep, development, courtship or migration. Fixed-length/support tests are software consistency checks, not empirical biomechanics.

sourceAssessment: Holthuis1987 selected text printed3–6 and actual neotype figure printed7 were inspected; NHM/OBIS/GBIF species hierarchy was checked. The original paper uses a historical broader Portunidae; current records retain Polybiidae. The retained Olivier Dugornay/Ifremer photograph was viewed separately.
fixesAfterRenderedReview: Added attached limb setae, larger chela finger bases, dark cutting tooth cues and longitudinal paddle ridges after the first rendered inspection.
Selected the detailed Holthuis asymmetry description while disclosing the equal-cheliped shorthand in MarLIN.
Reduced excessive shell specular gloss under compiled main-viewer lighting; recaptured and inspected all60 final Necora states.
